The possible meanings of the color keys are:

* Okay: The equipment is in a calibrated state.
* Not Okay: The equipment is not calibrated or is out of calibration.
* Out of Calibration: The equipment is no longer calibrated and requires recalibration.

These color keys provide a quick visual indication of the status of each piece of equipment, allowing for easy tracking and management of the calibration schedule.

results.question: What is the scope of the HACCP study for Poly Products Lamination?
results.expected_answer: Covers flexible packaging operations at Poly Products-Lamination (GH) Ltd, Spintex, Accra, from raw material reception (resins, films, inks) to finished flexible films, packing and dispatch to customer.
results.ollama_answer:
According to Source 2: Current HACCP MANUAL 3.10.2022 - Copy.xlsx, Sheet: FST members, Section: FST members, the scope of the HACCP study is:

"This study covers the flexible packaging operations in Poly Products-Lamination (GH) Limited located at Motorway Industrial Estate, Near Cocacola Bottling company , Spintex  , Accra; Postal Address: P.O Box 5334, Accra, Ghana – W/Africa from raw materials reception (resins, films, inks) to the finished product (flexible films) to packing and dispatch to customer."

This scope is also mentioned in Source 4: Current HACCP MANUAL 3.10.2022 - Copy.xlsx, Sheet: FST members, Section: Authorisation of finished study.

Therefore, the answer is that the scope of the HACCP study for Poly Products Lamination covers the flexible packaging operations from raw materials reception to the finished product, including packing and dispatch to customer.

These include rodents, snakes, flying and crawling insects and other pests. Hence pest control is an integral part of the organization’s activities.  7.1.2 Areas included in the pest control program are the production areas, offices, warehouses, canteen, stores and the general factory site and its immediate surroundings.  7.1.3 This is done on a regular basis to prevent contamination of products and food contact surfaces.  7.1.4 Poly Products shall engage the services of a qualified pest control agency/contractor to undertake the activity of controlling pests on site. In order to ensure a professional job, Poly Products shall ensure the pest control accredited agency is a registered company by law.   7.2 General Factory There shall be regular at least monthly spraying of the factory against mosquitoes, snakes and other crawling and flying insects. Pesticides shall be employed in this exercise.  7.3 Production Hall 7.3.1 Specific areas in the production hall shall be identified. These areas shall have traps to control rodents.  7.3.2 Insectocutors (special electrical equipment for killing flying insects) shall be installed for the control of insects and flies.  7.4 Offices Periodic disinfection and spraying of insecticides shall be done in offices as per the pest control schedule. All offices shall also have pest traps to control rodents where applicable.   7.5 Warehouses/Stores 7.5.1 All warehouses and stores for raw materials, packaging materials and finished goods shall be fitted with pest traps to control the activities of rodents.  7.5.2 These traps as well as those in other areas on the pest map shall be inspected on a weekly basis except weekends, holidays.  7.5.3 The purpose of this inspection is to pick up any dead rodents for disposal and subsequent replacement of baits, glue-boards as applicable.   7.6 Canteen 7.6.1 The presence of food residue and transient garbage makes the canteen susceptible to pest invasion, especially houseflies, cockroaches and rodents.   7.6.2 Rodent traps shall be placed at possible entry points in the canteen to control rodents. Insectocutors would be installed in the canteen to control houseflies.  7.6.3 Aerosols shall not be permitted in the canteen in order to avoid contamination of food.  7.6.4 The canteen shall be included in the periodic fumigation activity in order to control mosquitoes and cockroaches. All utensils and kitchen equipment including food contact surfaces shall be covered during the fumigation activity. After fumigation, utensils, equipment and food contact surfaces shall be washed and disinfected.  7.7 Approved Chemicals 7.7.1 The pest control contractor shall be asked to present all chemicals to be used for controlling pests on site together with the MSDS.  7.7.2 This shall include chemicals used to control mosquitoes, snakes, mice, rats and other rodents. The traps and or adhesives shall be placed at each of the bait stations identified.   7.7.6 Pest control agents, cleaners shall inspect the traps on a weekly basis whether any rodent or any other pest has been caught. If there is a rodent trapped, the pest would be picked up and disposed correctly. If it was the cleaner that sighted the pest, the pest control agents will be notified.  7.7.7 If there are no rodents, the personnel checks whether the secured bait is still there or not and if not a new bait is replaced  7.7.8 The Pest Control Agent shall submit monthly reports indicating all activities on site.  7.7.9 The report shall include the type of pesticides used, quantity, concentration used, where, when and how applied, target pests, number of pest traps replaced (if any).  7.8 Trigger Levels 7.8.1 The following activity below will serve as a trigger for the immediate intervention of an external pest controller. results.question: How is waste segregated and disposed of on site?
results.expected_answer: Waste categorised as plastic/PE film, general waste, and liquid waste; segregated daily; PE/trim/flexible film bagged; bins emptied at least once per shift or when full; liquid waste to septic tank cleared by 3rd-party contractor; labelled materials shredded before disposal.
results.ollama_answer:
According to the provided context, waste segregation and disposal are managed as follows:

* Waste is categorized into three types:
	+ Plastic waste (flexible films)
	+ General waste (including packages of consumables, food debris from canteen, and other office supplies)
	+ Liquid waste (from toilet facilities and main amenities)
* Containers for waste and inedible or hazardous substances are designed with the following standards and guidelines:
	+ Clearly identified for their various intended purposes
	+ Located in designated areas
	+ Constructed of impervious material that can be readily cleaned and sanitized
	+ Made up of lids that are closed when not in immediate use
	+ Segregated in a demarcated area where the waste may pose a risk to the product
* Liquid waste from toilet facilities and main amenities is channeled into a septic tank, which is regularly recovered and disposed of by a third-party liquid waste management contractor.
* Solid waste is segregated daily into general waste, PE waste for recycling, flexible waste for disfiguration and destruction, trim waste, plastic, and others. The PE, trim waste, and flexible film waste are disposed in plastic bags.
* Special bins that are durable to hold the various kinds of waste identified are positioned at areas where waste is generated.
* All labelled materials, products, or printed packaging materials are disfigured by cutting into shreds before disposal to ensure they cannot be reused or enter the supply chain again.
* Plastic waste containing PE is disposed to a contractor for recycling. Recycled plastic materials are not used on site at any stage of production.

Records of all waste removals and disposals are kept.

results.question: How does the facility control physical contamination from glass and brittle materials?
results.expected_answer: Periodic inspection of Perspex/glass machine coverings, monthly glass audits with corrective actions, and snap-off knife blades are forbidden.
results.ollama_answer:
According to Source 1: Current HACCP MANUAL 3.10.2022 - Copy.xlsx, Sheet: CROSS CONTAMINATION (2), Section: CROSS CONTAMINATION (2), the facility controls physical contamination from glass and brittle materials by:

* Periodic inspections are done to ensure coverings of machines made of brittle materials such as machine covering made of Perspex and glass components of equipment are intact. [Source 1, PPL PRPs, 1.3.1]
* Regular monthly glass audits are carried out and measures put in place to prevent, control or detect potential contamination and corrective actions put in place. [Source 1, PPL PRps, 1.3.2]

Additionally, according to Source 7: Current HACCP MANUAL 3.10.2022 - Copy.xlsx, Sheet: Hazard Analysis, Section: Hazard Analysis, the facility also controls physical contamination from dust and soil by:

* The use of snap off knife blade is forbidden. [Source 7, P8, SLITTING, Dust, physical]
* Tools are to be locked up in their respective tool boxes and must not be left loose in any place or on surfaces where product contamination can occur. [Source 1, PPL PRps, 1.3.4]

Overall, the facility has implemented measures to prevent and control physical contamination from glass and brittle materials, as well as dust and soil, through regular inspections, audits, and good manufacturing practices.

site plans and processing details are controlled. 7.2.3 Personnel Security Measures 7.2.3.1 Personnel security is taken seriously. Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place. results.question: How does the achievement rating scale convert to results in the KPI workbook?
results.expected_answer: Rating 1-5 maps to performance levels (e.g. 80/100/110/120) and weighted results such as 0.64, 0.80, 0.88, 0.96.
results.ollama_answer:

| Rating | Related Rating | Results |

| 1 | 0 | 0 |
| 2 | 80 | 0.64 |
| 3 | 100 | 0.8 |
| 4 | 110 | 0.88 |
| 5 | 120 | 0.96 |

The achievement rating scale converts to results as follows:

* Rating 1 (Does not meet all expectation) corresponds to a result of 0.
* Rating 2 (Meets some expectation) corresponds to a result of 0.64.
* Rating 3 (Meets all expectation) corresponds to a result of 0.8.
* Rating 4 (Exceeds some expectation) corresponds to a result of 0.88.
* Rating 5 (Exceeds all expectation) corresponds to a result of 0.96.

This conversion is used in the KPI workbook to evaluate employee performance and track progress towards achieving specific objectives.

results.question: What must be confirmed before a job enters production?
results.expected_answer: Carton internal dimensions checked, customer approval of dimensions, artwork checked internally and approved by customer, print capability approved, and paper combination determined and approved.
results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context documents (Sources 1-8), it can be inferred that the following requirements must be met before a job enters production:

* The term has a specific set of requirements to be met, and those requirements are not fully covered by the scope of the FSMS audit.
* The processes, products, or product groups must be described in detail when essential for food safety.
* The main activities and not obvious supporting activities (such as receiving raw materials, cooking batches of raw materials, human resources, etc.) must be defined to clarify what is meant by the term production.

These requirements are mentioned across multiple sources, including Sources 1-3, which provide guidance on scope statement guidance for FSMS. Additionally, Source 7, Current HACCP MANUAL 3.10.2022 - Copy.xlsx, mentions incident response security measures and personnel hygiene practices that must be followed before a job enters production.

Therefore, it can be concluded that the requirements mentioned above must be confirmed before a job enters production to ensure compliance with FSMS guidelines and maintain food safety standards.

Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place. * Compliance to applicable food laws: 1 / year + After every change in food law

results.question: What is our procedure for handling non-conforming raw material from an approved supplier? (cross-document)
results.expected_answer: Per HACCP PRP for Management of Purchased Materials: non-conforming items placed on-hold and rejected/returned to supplier (imported items sold to recyclers or destroyed under supervision); supplier notified and approval status reviewed.
results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context documents, our procedure for handling non-conforming raw material from an approved supplier can be summarized as follows:

* The supplier will be contacted and notified of the non-conformance.
* If the non-conformity involves product quality, the supplier will be required to reply with a plan to correct the issue.
* In cases where purchased items are imported, the supplier will be notified of the non-conformance after which the material is either sold to recycling plants (in the case of packaging) or destroyed under supervision (in the case of other items that cannot be recycled).
* The non-conforming product will be placed on-hold and rejected.
* Criteria for disqualification include:
	+ Lack of prompt response to complaint or problem identified by the supplier.
	+ Lack of supply of quality raw material in two successive instances without corrective actions.

This procedure is outlined in [Source 1: Current HACCP MANUAL 3.10.2022 - Copy.xlsx, Sheet: MGT OF PURCH MAT & SERV , Section: MGT OF PURCH MAT & SERV] under the "Management of Purchased Materials and Services" PRP (FS_PRP_06).

Additionally, [Source 1] also mentions that all non-conforming products are stored in demarcated storage areas and released to production for use only after verification of conformity with specified requirements.

It is important to note that this procedure applies to raw materials and packaging materials, as well as other items purchased from approved suppliers.
